Problem 904. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 4
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. The school must be on an end plot. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 6 km and two checkpoints are 3 cm apart.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=factory, B=homes, C=park, D=school. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. The school is on an end plot. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: 3×6=18 km.
Answer.
A=factory, B=homes, C=park, D=school is a valid assignment. Cross-domain answer: 18 km.
Knowledge takeaway.
A place can be unsuitable not because of its own properties, but because of what would be next to it.
Formal model.
Permutation CSP with all-different and adjacency/non-adjacency constraints.
Problem 905. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 5
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. The school must be on an end plot. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=school, B=park, C=homes, D=factory. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. The school is on an end plot. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Answer.
A=school, B=park, C=homes, D=factory is a valid assignment. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
A place can be unsuitable not because of its own properties, but because of what would be next to it.
Formal model.
Permutation CSP with all-different and adjacency/non-adjacency constraints.
N7. Natural risk: hazard, exposure, protection
Problem 906. Hazard, exposure, and protection: case 1
Knowledge context.
Natural risk depends on more than the physical hazard. Exposure and protective measures also affect outcomes.
Given facts.

For this classroom model, risk index = hazard × exposure ÷ protection. Data: Site A: hazard=2, exposure=4, protection=1; Site B: hazard=4, exposure=2, protection=2; Site C: hazard=3, exposure=3, protection=3.
Rules.
Use the formula exactly as stated. A higher hazard does not necessarily mean higher risk if exposure or protection differs.
Task.
Compute the risk index for each site. Which site has the lowest modeled risk?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Compute hazard×exposure÷protection for each site. 2. Results: A=8.00, B=4.00, C=3.00. 3. The lowest value is Site C.
Answer.
A=8.00; B=4.00; C=3.00. Lowest: Site C.
Knowledge takeaway.
Separating hazard from risk prevents the mistaken idea that the most dangerous process always creates the greatest overall risk.
Formal model.
Explicit risk-index function over three variables; compare computed values.
